Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I've been farming these fields for 45 years — I know every patch of them. Two of us in the household now, so labor is my biggest worry, not money. I'll hire help for the busy weeks.

**Land allocation.** 35 mu total. I keep about 25 mu in the wheat-maize rotation — that's my bread and butter, and the double crop gives me grain for the household plus income. The remaining 10 mu I keep in cotton. Cotton pays better per mu when the price holds, but it's a lot of work — picking especially — so I won't expand it at my age. I used to do 15-20 mu cotton when the kids were home, but not anymore.

**Wheat (25 mu).** I plant around October 10-15, right after maize harvest. I use Jimai-type improved variety, saved seed from last year plus some new seed I buy every 2-3 years to refresh. For fertilizer — based on my yield last year (about 480 kg/mu) and the soil looking decent, I plan roughly 16 kg N/mu total, split base and topdress. Base application is compound fertilizer (15-15-15) about 40 kg/mu before plowing, then I topdress urea around jointing in March, another 10-12 kg urea/mu. Phosphorus and potassium come mostly from the compound. I irrigate 3-4 times: overwintering water in late November if it's dry, then jointing, heading, and filling. Groundwater is getting expensive and the table keeps dropping — I don't waste it. Spray herbicide once in spring for broadleaf weeds, and watch for aphids and stripe rust around heading.

**Maize (25 mu, same fields).** Plant immediately after wheat harvest — June 12-15, no-till directly into wheat stubble to save those precious days. Use Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid — I don't save maize seed, always buy fresh. Base fertilizer goes on with the planter, about 30 kg of compound/mu, then topdress urea 15 kg/mu at large-flare stage (V8 or so). Total N around 14-15 kg/mu. Usually I only irrigate once or twice — at silking if July is dry, and maybe one more at grain fill. The rains in August usually cover the rest. Harvest late September. I expect about 500 kg/mu if it's a normal year.

**Cotton (10 mu).** This is the trickier crop. Plant around April 20-25 under mulch film. I use a locally adapted improved variety. Cotton needs less N than people think — too much and it just grows tall and doesn't set bolls. I plan about 13 kg N/mu, plus phosphorus and potassium because potassium matters for boll quality. Apply base fertilizer before ridging, topdress at squaring and again at flowering. Irrigate 2 times usually — at squaring and flowering. Spray insecticide 4-5 times through the season for bollworm and aphids, and a PGR (mepiquat chloride) 2-3 times to control growth. Picking starts mid-September and goes through October — this is where I'll need to hire pickers, probably 15-20 hired days because my wife and I can't do 10 mu ourselves anymore.

**Cost and cash.** Inputs will run roughly 350-400 yuan/mu for wheat, 280-320 for maize, 600+ for cotton. I can cover it from last year's grain sale proceeds. I keep some cash reserve for a bad year — never spend it all on inputs.
